title: Why Does Google Pay Apple $20 Billion a Year?
description:
Google paid Apple about $20 billion in 2022 just to stay the default search engine in Safari, and Apple keeps 36% of the ad money from those searches.
#apple #google #money #shorts

Sources: MacRumors (Aug 5, 2024; Sep 2, 2025; Oct 27, 2022); Yahoo Finance via AOL (2025); Engadget (Nov 13, 2023); Search Engine Land (2023, 2025); 9to5Mac (Sep 3, 2025); iClarified (Sep 3, 2025); Business Insider via Yahoo (Dec 6, 2025); PYMNTS (Feb 4, 2026); Apple Q4 FY2022 results
Photos: psd, Janitors, Carlos Luna, bluesparknz, rpongsaj (CC BY, Flickr)
first_comment: Be honest: have you ever changed your phone's default search engine, or never touched it? 🔍

scenes.say: Google pays Apple {$20 billion|twenty billion dollars} for one setting.
scenes.source: MacRumors Aug 5 2024 ('In 2022, Google paid Apple $20 billion', per the DOJ in the antitrust case); Yahoo Finance via AOL 2025 ('the $20 billion figure is an estimate for 2022 found in the antitrust court documents'); MacRumors Sep 2 2025 (~$20B annually)

scenes.say: The search bar in Safari, on every iPhone.
scenes.source: Google is the default search engine in Safari on iPhone (MacRumors Sep 2 2025; Engadget Nov 2023)

scenes.say: Court documents put the {2022|twenty twenty two} check at {$20 billion|twenty billion}.
scenes.source: Yahoo Finance via AOL 2025; MacRumors Aug 5 2024

scenes.say: Apple also keeps {36%|thirty six percent} of the ad money from those searches.
scenes.source: Engadget Nov 13 2023 (Kevin Murphy testimony; Pichai confirmed 36%); Search Engine Land 2023 ('Google CEO Sundar Pichai has confirmed that the company pays Apple 36% of its Safari search revenue')

scenes.say: {$20 billion|Twenty billion}, next to {$78 billion|seventy eight billion} for all of Apple's services. About a quarter.
scenes.source: MacRumors Oct 27 2022 + Apple Q4 FY2022 results (services revenue $78B in fiscal 2022); $20B / $78B = 26%

scenes.say: But you can switch search engines in a few taps. So why pay?
scenes.source: Safari lets users pick Google, Yahoo, Bing, DuckDuckGo or Ecosia under Settings > Safari > Search Engine (Apple support)

scenes.say: Because Google is betting you'll never change it. It's called the default effect.
In {2025|twenty twenty five}, a judge banned exclusive deals, but let the payments keep coming.
scenes.source: MacRumors Sep 2 2025 ('not allowed to enter into exclusive contracts... still allowed to pay Apple'); iClarified Sep 3 2025 (court rejected a ban on payments); PYMNTS Feb 4 2026 (appeals pending, payments not blocked)

scenes.say: So every time you search on your iPhone, you're the reason
